visual_text: Going with a parent to an appointment
She has been dizzy in the mornings.
Without a plan, the daughter answers for her mother.
I will tell her about the mornings.
And I will add anything you miss.
The evening before, they agree who says what.
In the room, the daughter asks what her mother thinks.
Agree beforehand who says what. Ask questions that let them speak.
Clayman et al, 2005; Laidsaar-Powell et al, 2013
alt_text: Illustrative three-panel comic. Panel 1: in a clinic, a daughter answers for her older mother, who looks down; a doctor sits at a desk. Panel 2: the evening before, at a kitchen table, they agree who says what. Panel 3: the daughter asks "What do you think, Mum?" In a US study of 93 visits, patients took part more when companions asked what they thought. A link, not proof.
